description_full: EQT Corporation engages in the exploration, production, gathering, and transmission of hydrocarbons and natural gas. The company sells natural gas, natural gas liquids, and oil to marketers, utilities, and industrial customers located in the Appalachian Basin. It also provides marketing services and contractual pipeline capacity management services, as well as engages in risk management and hedging activities. In addition, it owns and operates propane storage and distribution terminals. The company was formerly known as Equitable Resources Inc. and changed its name to EQT Corporation in February 2009. EQT Corporation was founded in 1888 and is headquartered in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: EQT Corporation is a large-cap energy business with a $33.0B market cap on $8.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and +14% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $2.8B in free cash flow — roughly 33 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.51× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.3× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 7.4×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
